chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abi Ayyub, from Abi Basir, who said:
I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about a people who accompanied one another as companions on their journey, and some of them stole the belongings of others.
So he said: "This is a betrayer; his hand is not cut off, but he is to be pursued on account of his theft and his betrayal."

It was said to him: Then if he steals from his father's house? He said: "His hand is not cut off, because a man's son is not barred from entering his father's house. This is a betrayer. Likewise, if he steals from a house belonging to his brother or his sister, when he used to enter upon them and they did not prevent him from entering."

key_terms.بِسَرِقَتِهِ: for his theft; referring to the act for which he is held accountable
key_terms.خَائِنٌ: a betrayer; one who violates trust rather than committing a qualifying theft for hadd punishment
key_terms.خِيَانَتِهِ: his betrayal; breach of trust in a setting of permitted access
key_terms.لَا يُقْطَعُ: the hadd punishment of amputation is not carried out
key_terms.مَنْزِلِ أَبِيهِ: his father's house; a place the son is not ordinarily barred from entering
key_terms.يُحْجَبُ: to be prevented or barred; indicating restricted access relevant to the legal ruling

ai.seo_question: Does the hadd punishment for theft apply when someone steals from a companion or from a family member's house?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning theft committed in situations of trusted access, such as among travel companions or within the homes of close family members. Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام distinguishes such cases from the category of theft requiring amputation, describing them instead as betrayal and treachery due to the absence of barred access.
